name: Zethar
title: One of King Ahasuerus's seven court officials
summary: Zethar was one of the seven court officials (eunuchs) who served at the court of King Ahasuerus (Xerxes) in the Persian Empire. He is mentioned in the Book of Esther as one of the trusted servants whom the king sent to bring Queen Vashti during the great banquet. Although his role in the Bible is brief, he represents the structure and power of the Persian court.

keyEvents.title: Service at King Ahasuerus's banquet
keyEvents.description: Zethar is mentioned as one of the seven court officials who served at King Ahasuerus's great banquet in the citadel of Susa, which lasted 180 days.

keyEvents.title: Sent to fetch Queen Vashti
keyEvents.description: On the seventh day of the feast, when the king was merry with wine, he commanded Zethar and the six other courtiers to bring Queen Vashti wearing the royal crown, so that her beauty might be shown to the people.

keyEvents.title: Queen Vashti's Refusal
keyEvents.description: Queen Vashti refused to come when Zethar and the other courtiers delivered the king's command, which led to a serious political crisis at the court.

keyEvents.title: The Consequences of Vashti's Disobedience
keyEvents.description: Vashti's refusal of the message brought by Zethar and the other courtiers caused the king to consult his wise men, and Vashti was ultimately deposed as queen.
